prompt: Split a list into consecutive batches of at most a given size. Complete batch so every batch is a new ArrayList and the final batch may be short.
explanation: Stepping the loop index by size instead of by 1 lands you on the first element of each batch in turn. The end of a batch is the smaller of start + size and the list size, which is what lets the last batch be short without any special case. Copying elements into a fresh ArrayList for each batch keeps the result independent of the input list.
hints: Advance the outer loop by size each time (start += size) so each pass begins at the next batch.
The end of a batch is Math.min(start + size, items.size()) -- that one line is what makes the last batch come out short instead of running off the end.
Create a new ArrayList inside the loop for each batch and add it to the result before moving on.
